image_description: A close-up view of a motorcycle front wheel assembly featuring a dual-disc braking system. The image shows two perforated metal rotors, silver calipers with yellow accents, black suspension forks, and a portion of the tire. There is visible text overlay in the center.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct circular rotors are clearly visible, exhibiting the correct aspect ratio of large diameter to thin profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Silver metallic caliper assemblies are correctly positioned straddling the outer edges of the rotors.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central wheel hub area is heavily occluded by the fork lowers, axle assembly, and camera angle; specific lug bolts are not discernible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors appear to be floating discs with visible mounting bobbins/spiders connecting the braking surface to the carrier, consistent with ventilated motorcycle disc construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark rectangular shapes consistent with brake pads are visible inside the caliper jaws, contacting the rotor surface.
Black hydraulic hoses are visible entering the top of the caliper assemblies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors feature a distinct pattern of circular drill holes near the perimeter, matching the 'cross-drilled' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotors appear uniformly silver/metallic without significant blueing or brown heat staining, suggesting they are new or lightly used.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The calipers exhibit a metallic sheen and casting lines typical of machined aluminum alloy components.

artifact_observations.location: Center of the image, overlaying the brake assembly
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is faint, semi-transparent white text overlaid on the image (likely a watermark). The characters are indistinct and do not form clear readable words, typical of AI-generated artifacts or low-quality compression artifacts mimicking watermarks.
The yellow surface lacks realistic plastic texture or reflection detail, appearing slightly smudged or 'painted on' compared to the sharpness of the mechanical parts.

artifact_observations.location: Connection points of the floating disc bobbins
artifact_observations.reasoning: The small metal bobbins connecting the inner and outer rotor rings are slightly ill-defined and lack precise geometric clarity, blending slightly into the background.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomy of the braking system and distinguish it from generic car brakes or other mechanical parts.
To verify the physical separation between the caliper, rotor, and fork tubes, ensuring no impossible fusion or depth flattening.
To check if the drilled holes in the rotor are clean circles or if they suffer from melting/distortion at the boundaries.
To analyze the illegible text artifact identified in the center of the image.
To assess general sharpness, lighting consistency, and noise levels.

focus_areas: Integrity of rotor drill hole geometry
Legibility and nature of central text overlay
Texture realism of metallic surfaces vs. plastic components
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'floating' nature of the brake discs. In AI images, the small bobbins connecting the disc layers often melt or fail to connect properly. Also, scrutinize the text overlay—is it a real watermark added post-generation, or an AI hallucination? If it's gibberish, it counts as an artifact.
